purpose: Independent practice of B1.2 — composing and decomposing numbers to 50 in multiple ways.
student_learning_goal: I can compose and decompose any number to 50 using tens, ones, and partner pairs in different ways.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can compose and decompose any number to 50 using tens, ones, and partner pairs in different ways.
header.character_watermark: Otto in the top-right corner, holding two jars of marbles. Small (~1.5in tall).

parts.part_title: Part 1: Tens and Ones, Then a New Way
parts.student_instructions: For each target number, write ONE tens-and-ones decomposition AND ONE different decomposition.
parts.visual_layout: Top third of the page. Three rows. Each row shows a target number on the left (15, 27, 42), a tens-and-ones blank on the middle (___ tens + ___ ones), and a free-form blank on the right ('Another way: ___ + ___').

image_placeholders.description: A 3-row decomposition grid in B&W line-art. Left column: target numbers 15, 27, 42 (each in a bold box). Middle column: tens-and-ones template '___ tens + ___ ones'. Right column: 'Another way: ___ + ___'. Each row ~1.2in tall.
image_placeholders.placement: Top third of the page; full-width.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS03_P1_DECOMP_GRID: keywords (tens, ones, decomposition) name what the grid asks for.

parts.answer_key: 15: tens=1, ones=5. Another way: 7+8 or 10+5 or 12+3 etc. 27: tens=2, ones=7. Another way: 15+12 or 20+7 or 25+2 etc. 42: tens=4, ones=2. Another way: 20+22 or 25+17 or 40+2 etc.

parts.part_title: Part 2: Three Ways for 32 and Three Ways for 47
parts.student_instructions: Find three different partner pairs for each target.
parts.visual_layout: Middle of the page. Two compose tasks side by side. Task A: '32 = ___ + ___' three times. Task B: '47 = ___ + ___' three times.

image_placeholders.description: Two stacked compose tasks in B&W line-art. Task A: header '32 = ___ + ___' three times in a column. Task B: header '47 = ___ + ___' three times. Each compose blank ~2in wide. Total grid spans full width.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS03_P2_COMPOSE_TASKS: keywords (partner, pairs, compose) name what the task asks for.

parts.part_title: Part 3: As Many Ways As You Can
parts.student_instructions: Pick a number between 25 and 50. Find as many decompositions as you can.
parts.visual_layout: Bottom of the page. A target box at the top ('My number: ___'). Below it, 6 blank lines for decompositions. To the right, a small Otto puppet thumbnail with a thought bubble: 'Otto bets you can find 5 or more!'

image_placeholders.description: An open decomposition area in B&W line-art. Top: small target box 'My number: ___'. Below: 6 blank lines for decompositions. Right side: Otto puppet (~1.5in tall) with a thought bubble.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS03_P3_OPEN_DECOMP: keywords (decomposition, otto, number) name what the area asks for.

parts.answer_key: Open. Accept any target 25-50 with at least 4 decompositions. Children with 5+ decompositions including non-tens-ones partners are demonstrating mastery.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, flip the page over and try a number BIGGER than 50 (like 75 or 99). How many decompositions can you find?
teacher_notes: Lesson 3 consolidation; this is the keystone worksheet for B1.2. Hand out at the end of small-group time. Watch for: (a) Part 1 children who write the SAME thing in both columns — they haven't internalised that there are multiple decompositions; (b) Part 3 children who only find tens-and-ones decompositions — flag for the rod-moving reteach in Day 4 small groups. Use Part 3 as evidence for the formative tracker column 'finds non-tens-ones partner pair'.
